nota.t: Scientific investigation
Variables are manipulated (the changed), reacted (the observed) and constant (the fixed).
We organise the data in tables and graphs.
Five senses
Science process skills

baris: use the senses to gather information
separate things according to the same characteristics
make measurements with the correct tools and units
make preliminary conclusions based on observations
make an expectation about something that will happen
convey information in the form of tables, graphs or verbally
describe the change of something over time
determine what is changed, observed and fixed

glosari: Factors that can change in an investigation.
A general testable statement about the relationship of variables.

nota.t: Rules and safety
Follow the rules; handle the apparatus carefully; report an accident.
Skeletal system
The skeleton supports the body, gives shape and protects the internal organs.
Movement
Bones, muscles and joints work together for movement.

glosari: The arrangement of bones in the body.
Tissues that contract and relax to move bones.

nota.t: Animal respiratory organs
Life cycle
butterfly: egg → larva (caterpillar) → pupa → butterfly · frog: egg → tadpole → young frog → frog

glosari: A small hole in the insect's body for breathing.
The stages in an animal's life.

nota.t: Plants respond
Plants react to light, water, gravity and touch.
Shoots grow towards light · Roots grow towards water and gravity · Leaves also contract when touched
Breeding
Seeds are spread by wind, water, animals and explosion.

glosari: How seeds are carried to other places.

nota.t: Standard units
Points should line up with the reading to avoid errors.

glosari: The same unit of measurement around the world.
Reading error due to incorrect eye position.

nota.t: Floating and sinking
Objects less dense than water will float. Objects that are dense will sink.
wood, cork, plastic ball → float · stone, marble, nail → sink
Liquid
Oil floats on water because oil is less dense than water.

glosari: A measure of how dense a material is.
Being on the surface of the liquid.

nota.t: Test with litmus paper
Acid: lemon juice, vinegar · Alkaline: soapy water, toothpaste · Neutral: distilled water, sugar water
Acidic substances taste sour; alkaline substances feel bitter and smooth. Do not taste the material in the laboratory.

glosari: Indicator paper to test acid or alkali.

nota.t: Members of the Solar System
Sun in the middle. Eight planets in order: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune.
Largest planet: Jupiter · Smallest planet: Mercury · Nearest planet to the Sun: Mercury
Earth and Moon
The Earth rotates on its axis (day and night) and revolves around the Sun. The moon revolves around the Earth.

glosari: A large object orbiting the Sun.
An imaginary line where something rotates.
Paths of objects around other objects.

nota.t: A simple machine
Machines make work easier. Examples of simple machines: lever, pulley, wheel and axle, inclined plane, wedge, screw.

glosari: A simple tool that makes work easier.
A combination of two or more simple machines.
